findings.title: Dataset field-size report omits JSON key and framing bytes
findings.what: fieldSizes serializes each top-level value in isolation and sums those byte counts, but presents the result as total dataset.json bytes and derives every share from it. Top-level key strings, colons, commas, and object braces are absent. At the immutable baseline `{a:1}` is reported as 1 byte and 100 percent for `a`, while its UTF-8 JSON body is 7 bytes, so the report is not reproducible from the claimed wire artifact.
findings.fix: Make totalBytes equal the UTF-8 byte length of the serialized dataset and account for each serialized key plus separators and framing, either by assigning overhead deterministically to fields or reporting an explicit framing row; derive percentages from that true total.
findings.acceptance: Tests assert that totalBytes equals Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(dataset), `utf8`) for one-field, multi-field, multibyte-key/value, and undefined-property fixtures, and that all reported attribution including framing sums exactly to the same total.
findings.verifyNote: A direct baseline call with `{a:1}` returned totalBytes=1, while Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify({a:1}), `utf8`) returned 7. Lines 43-55 sum valueBytes only, and the test at lines 35-39 merely re-sums those same rows, so it cannot detect the omitted wire bytes.
